business_problem: MediaTek needed a secure and scalable way to train and serve very large language models, support internal AI assistants for engineering work, and manage thousands of monthly training iterations without exposing proprietary data or overwhelming its infrastructure team.
solution_summary: MediaTek centralized its AI initiatives in an on-premises AI factory powered by NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD and supporting DGX systems. The environment gives the semiconductor company a secure place to train Breeze models and a 480B-parameter traditional-Chinese model, run a centralized inference API, distill smaller versions for edge and mobile use, and power internal tools such as AI-assisted code completion and automated documentation. NVIDIA AI Enterprise components, including NIM, Riva, NeMo, and TensorRT-LLM, improve inference speed and throughput, while NVIDIA Mission Control consolidates GPU provisioning, Linux cluster deployment, health checks, and utilization monitoring for the DGX SuperPOD. The result is a full-stack AI platform that lets MediaTek run larger models, more iterations, and more local experimentation without sending sensitive design data outside the company.

data_flow: Internal engineering data and LLM training corpora are processed inside MediaTek's DGX SuperPOD AI factory, tuned with NeMo, served through NIM and Riva, accelerated by TensorRT-LLM, and monitored through Mission Control for both internal productivity tools and centralized model APIs.
business_outcome: MediaTek processes about 60 billion inference tokens a month, completes more than 24,000 training iterations each month, trains 480B+ parameter models in one week, improves inference speed by 40% with a 60% token-throughput gain, and reduces documentation cycles from weeks to days.
